title: Practical: Collection Utilities Module
story: Every program needs to find min, max, filter, and map over collections. Instead of rewriting these loops every time, build a reusable collection utilities module with generic functions that work on any Vec[T].
why: A collection utilities module provides generic operations that work across any Vec type, saving you from rewriting loop patterns repeatedly.
analogy: A toolkit has pliers, screwdrivers, and a hammer — tools that work on any screw, any nail, any bolt regardless of brand. Collection utilities are your toolkit for Vecs: find_max doesn't care if it's a Vec of numbers, strings, or anything — it just works.
try_it: Add `fold[T, U]` that reduces a Vec into a single value using an accumulator function. Use it to sum numbers and concatenate strings. Add `first_where` that finds the index of the first item matching a predicate.
tips: Pass comparison functions as parameters for maximum flexibility
Return Option when a result might not exist (empty Vec, no match)
Make functions generic so they work on Vec[Int], Vec[Str], Vec[YourType]
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle empty collections — always check len() == 0
Calling .clone() unnecessarily on Copy types like Int
Writing type-specific versions when a generic version would work
